text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonia signed an agreement on cooperation with the European Union in Luxembourg Tuesday which will enter into force on August 1.
- President of the European commission Hans van den Broek said the signing of the EU cooperation agreement will open new possibilities for Macedonia.
- Multinational military exercise Savior 97 to be held in Macedonia from May 12 to 16.

- Owner of the bankrupt financial institution TAT from Bitola Sonja Nikolovska will not participate in the protest rally of bank depositors. She said she would later give her explanations for TAT's bankruptcy.

- Speaking to state trade unions Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov said: "After independence Macedonia passed through a difficult but very significant period because we survived. We took care to keep as many people as possible in their jobs and in factories that could continue working under difficult conditions."

- The police dismantled tents rigged in front of parliament by independent trade unions who have been demonstrating and on a hunger strike for almost one month demanding work and better social conditions. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
